title: Expression of the High-affinity Neurotensin Receptor Defines an Immune‑cold, Poor‑prognosis Colorectal Cancer Subtype.
authors: Wu, Haoming; Wang, Yang; Song, Jun; Yan, Baoxiang; Wang, Chi; Liu, Jinpeng; He, Daheng; Weiss, Heidi L; Rychahou, Piotr; Banerjee, Moumita; Li, Jing; Evers, B Mark
one_liner_zh: 该文研究NTSR1在结直肠癌中塑造免疫冷微环境及T细胞排斥的机制，虽涉及转录因子下调，但核心是肿瘤免疫与临床预后，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: OBJECTIVE: We investigated neurotensin receptor 1 (NTSR1) as a potential mediator of the mechanical immune barrier that contributes to T-cell exclusion. SUMMARY BACKGROUND DATA: The efficacy of immunotherapy in advanced colorectal cancer (CRC) is limited by primary resistance, frequently characterized by an "immune-excluded" phenotype where physical and biological barriers prevent effector T-cell infiltration. Through its high-affinity receptor, NTSR1, neurotensin signaling has been implicated in tumor progression, yet its role in shaping the immune landscape of CRC remains unclear. METHODS: We integrated transcriptomic and clinical data from The Cancer Genome Atlas discovery cohort with an independent surgical validation cohort from the University of Kentucky. Random Forest machine learning identified molecular features associated with NTS/NTSR1 signaling, and a 3D tumor spheroid co-culture model was used to evaluate the impact of NTS/NTSR1 signaling on spatial T-cell distribution in vitro . RESULTS: Dual-cohort analyses revealed high NTSR1 expression as an independent risk factor for progression-free interval in the discovery cohort and overall survival in the validation cohort. Mechanistically, the NTS/NTSR1 axis upregulates a mechano-structural network centered on PLXNB3, FLNC, and AHNAK2, while simultaneously driving epithelial dedifferentiation through downregulation of core transcription factors (CDX2, SATB2). Together, these transcriptional programs are associated with the remodeling of the tumor microenvironment into an immune-cold, suppressive state. Moreover, 3D modeling indicated that ligand-activated NTS/NTSR1 signaling restricts T-cell infiltration, which was significantly reversed by the NTSR1 antagonist SR48692, providing functional support for a mechanical immune barrier proposed based on transcriptomic remodeling. CONCLUSIONS: Targeting the NTS/NTSR1 axis may attenuate biological and physical barriers underlying immune exclusion, providing a preclinical rationale for converting immune-excluded CRCs into immune-responsive tumors.
abstract_zh: 目的：我们研究了神经降压素受体1（NTSR1）作为机械性免疫屏障的潜在介导因子，该屏障有助于T细胞排斥。背景数据摘要：晚期结直肠癌（CRC）免疫治疗的疗效受原发性耐药限制，通常表现为“免疫排斥”表型，其中物理和生物屏障阻止效应T细胞浸润。通过其高亲和力受体NTSR1，神经降压素信号传导已被涉及肿瘤进展，但其在塑造CRC免疫微环境中的作用仍不清楚。方法：我们将癌症基因组图谱发现队列的转录组和临床数据与肯塔基大学的独立手术验证队列相结合。随机森林机器学习识别了与NTS/NTSR1信号传导相关的分子特征，并使用3D肿瘤球体共培养模型评估NTS/NTSR1信号传导对体外空间T细胞分布的影响。结果：双队列分析显示，高NTSR1表达是发现队列中无进展间期和验证队列中总生存期的独立风险因素。机制上，NTS/NTSR1轴上调以PLXNB3、FLNC和AHNAK2为中心的机械结构网络，同时通过下调核心转录因子（CDX2、SATB2）驱动上皮去分化。这些转录程序共同与肿瘤微环境重塑为免疫冷、抑制状态相关。此外，3D模型表明，配体激活的NTS/NTSR1信号传导限制T细胞浸润，而NTSR1拮抗剂SR48692显著逆转了这一效应，为基于转录组重塑提出的机械性免疫屏障提供了功能支持。结论：靶向NTS/NTSR1轴可能减弱免疫排斥背后的生物和物理屏障，为将免疫排斥型CRC转化为免疫反应性肿瘤提供了临床前依据。
